title: Addendum: replicate the chip-to-animal behaviour and bridge predictions on the male CNS (SIMULATED)
status: registered before any MaleCNS simulation was run, and before the FlyWire sweep's results were read
seen_before_registration: MaleCNS annotation and transmitter tables (counts, status labels, cell-type names); no connectivity read, nothing simulated
FlyWire quick run (3 conditions, 2 trials): vehicle MN9|sugar 81.5 Hz, gaba_block 0.2 152 Hz, ach_block 0.4 0 Hz

design.connectome: MaleCNS v1.0 flat connectome, minconf 0.5, brain and nerve cord
design.sign: consensus_nt from body-neurotransmitters: gaba and glutamate -1 (as Shiu et al.), histamine -1 (HisCl) but in no knob's class; every other or missing label +1
design.constants: Shiu et al. constants unchanged, including w_syn; synapse count is the weights file's weight
design.neuron_sets: each FlyWire set matched by cell type: a MaleCNS body belongs if its type equals the FlyWire cell_type of a set member, on the side letter of that member's FlyWire side (left -> L, right -> R; rootSide for sensory neurons, somaSide otherwise)
design.readout_neurons: MN9, aBN1 (SAD093) and aDN1 (DNg62) matched the same way; where two bodies match one FlyWire neuron, the one on the matched side is read
design.array: 544 single-unit electrodes drawn at random (seed 0) from cb_intrinsic neurons: MaleCNS publishes no per-neuron neuropil table among the files fetched
design.conditions: the 21 drug conditions and vehicle of the parent registration

M0_feeding_circuit_exists.statement: Sugar GRNs drive MN9 in the male CNS model as in FlyWire
M0_feeding_circuit_exists.test: MN9|sugar (vehicle) >= 20 Hz and MN9|sugar+bitter <= 0.5 x MN9|sugar

M_B1.test: Spearman(block fraction, MN9|sugar+bitter) over vehicle + 5 gaba_block levels >= 0.8

M_B2.test: Spearman(block fraction, readout) <= -0.8 for MN9|sugar and aBN1|JO-CE

M_C1.test: Spearman(|delta log2 mfr|, disruption index) >= 0.6 over the 21 drug conditions

reporting: Each prediction is reported with its value and pass/fail. A failed M0 means the matched circuit is not the same, and M_B1-M_C1 are then reported as uninterpretable rather than as failures of the bridge.
